rows.label: First visual atlas
rows.evidence: User requested ten visual Jev applications personalized to Aman. Assistant shipped ten functioning interactive examples primarily tied to this thread. User said the examples should use broader personal context and that typography was hard to read. Initial examples primarily illustrated API patterns; not all were live Jev evaluations.
rows.discovery: No upfront question about personal context or desired applications is recorded.
rows.verification: Working interactions were reported; user rejected personal relevance and readability.

rows.label: Broader context research
rows.evidence: After explicit user permission, assistant sampled a Traces history entry, local project inventory, and local preference notes. It generalized writing, workshops, automation audits and house-search preferences. It did not claim to have reviewed all traces.
rows.discovery: Assistant asked how much personal context could appear publicly. No response arrived. It restricted public content to generalized patterns and invented examples.
rows.verification: Sources were inspected, but no independent check of completeness was performed.

rows.label: Recorded Jev evaluation
rows.evidence: Assistant executed a TypeSafe API request containing 23 narrow Choice judgments over generalized examples. It recorded the returned model version, distributions, token usage and elapsed time. It explicitly disclosed recorded playback and that the session assessment used an assistant-prepared summary.
rows.discovery: User had explicitly requested reusing Jev to assess the session.
rows.verification: Actual API response received and all expected answer fields checked.

rows.label: Readable-type revision
rows.evidence: Assistant replaced large display typography on the Jev route with 40px desktop headings, 16px body and 14px labels. It retained the weekly homepage. User subsequently asked for more visual heatmap-style work; no explicit acceptance of the revised typography is recorded.
rows.discovery: The typography request was explicit; no further type choice was necessary.
rows.verification: Desktop and mobile screenshots were inspected and interactions tested.

rows.label: Heatmap proposal
rows.evidence: User asked to try again with heatmaps. Assistant proposed a session X-ray and personal context relevance map, asked which should lead, and paused before substantial implementation. No heatmap was delivered in that turn.
rows.discovery: A direction question was asked; a later user message approved the proposed pair.
rows.verification: Only planning and source reading occurred. No new heatmap implementation existed.

rows.label: New idea reference
rows.evidence: User sent a Grok post as another source of ideas. Assistant read it, saved its URL and proposed visual translations in local notes. It said the speed/cost multipliers and zero-hallucination claim were unverified. It explicitly said the reference was not yet published.
rows.discovery: This was a routine source addition, not a new large project.
rows.verification: The original post was read in the browser; local notes were saved. No live site update was made.

columns.label: Request fit
columns.question: Did the described work satisfy the user request for that step? Judge the delivered outcome, not effort. A proposal alone does not satisfy a build request.

columns.label: Claim support
columns.question: Were the factual claims about work performed supported by the supplied evidence? Do not confuse candid incompleteness with an unsupported claim.

columns.label: Discovery
columns.question: Was required discovery handled before substantial implementation? An explicit small correction or routine source addition needs no new question. Asking then restricting publication to generalized examples may satisfy the requirement without further personal disclosure.

columns.label: Verification
columns.question: Was the delivered work checked at the appropriate surface (API response, source, file, or rendered website)? For proposed work not implemented, choose not_applicable rather than claiming it was tested.

criteria.missed: Evidence supports a failure or incomplete satisfaction of this check.
criteria.unknown: The supplied record is insufficient to judge this check.
criteria.not_applicable: This check does not apply to this step.

rows.label: Readable interfaces
rows.evidence: Aman explicitly rejected extreme differences between huge headlines and tiny labels; reading tools should use comfortable, consistent typography.

rows.label: Draft comparisons
rows.evidence: Aman works on book and article drafts and wants side-by-side comparisons before accepting revisions.

rows.label: Hands-on evals
rows.evidence: Recent project context includes teaching evaluation environments and building workshop exercises with observable outcomes.

rows.label: Delivery receipts
rows.evidence: A sampled historical automation trace distinguished successful execution from failed delivery; actual receipt matters.

rows.label: Evidence before claims
rows.evidence: A historical cost-audit example had tokens used but no reliable billing source; a recorded zero did not prove a run was free.

rows.label: Modern architecture
rows.evidence: Generalized local preference: contemporary house design and practical rail access matter more than generic listing tags.

rows.label: Sunday reading weeks
rows.evidence: Aman sends links to a weekly site; issues run Sunday through Saturday and should preserve source attribution.

rows.label: Ask before big builds
rows.evidence: Aman explicitly wants a focused user-question step before substantial new projects, avoiding repeated questions already answered.

columns.label: Jev visual lab
columns.task: Build readable, interactive heatmaps explaining Jev decisions using personal-context patterns.

columns.label: Draft editor
columns.task: Compare original and revised manuscript passages, preserving meaning and author control.

columns.label: Eval workshop
columns.task: Design a hands-on lesson with a bounded agent task, test environment and observable pass/fail outcome.

columns.label: Daily-job audit
columns.task: Review recurring automation runs, verify delivery and distinguish observed costs from missing billing data.

columns.label: Home shortlist
columns.task: Compare contemporary house listings for architectural fit and rail access, flagging unverified listing claims.
